gloss: first three days of the New Year

definitions.gloss: first three days of the New Year (January 1-3)
definitions.explanation: The first three days of January, considered the core of the New Year holiday period in Japan. Most businesses are closed, and families gather for traditional celebrations.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}が{日|にち}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{実家|じっか}→実家：03076_jikka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{過|す}ごす→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧。
examples.english: I spend the first three days of the year at my parents' house.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}が{日|にち}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦お{店|みせ}→お店：21164_omise⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{閉|し}まっている→閉まる：00754_shimaru⟧。
examples.english: Shops are closed during the first three days of the year.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}が{日|にち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{過|す}ぎる→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦ずつ→〜ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧⟦{普段|ふだん}→普段：00041_fudan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{様子|ようす}→様子：01521_yousu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{戻|もど}って→戻る：01117_modoru⟧いく。
examples.english: After the first three days, the town gradually returns to its usual routine.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{三|さん}が{日|にち} (January 1-3) is the most important holiday period in Japan. During this time, families visit shrines (⟦{初詣|はつもうで}→初詣：05804_hatsumoude⟧), eat traditional New Year dishes ({御節料理|おせちりょうり}), and exchange greetings. Most businesses and government offices are closed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧{三|さん}が{日|にち}: the first three days of the New Year
- {三|さん}が{日|にち}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧: during the first three days

WRITING:
The ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ in {三|さん}が{日|にち} is usually written in hiragana. The word derives from {三箇日|さんがにち} where {箇|か} is a counter.
